findings.evidence: Basic.lean:126-127; `grep -n 'mul_div_cancel\b' mathlib/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Basic.lean` → line 962 `theorem mul_div_cancel (a b : G) : a * (b / a) = b`, the `@[to_additive]` source of `add_sub_cancel`.
findings.fix: Extract `theorem smul_add_one_sub_smul (z : ℝ) (p : V) : z • p + (1 - z) • p = p := by module` (or `by rw [← add_smul]; simp`) and reduce `sum_splitCollinear` to `rw [splitCollinear_def, Multiset.sum_cons, Multiset.sum_cons, ← add_assoc, smul_add_one_sub_smul, ← Multiset.sum_cons, Multiset.cons_erase hp]`. Same pattern, lighter: `card_splitCollinear` (lines 117-120) can be `simp [splitCollinear_def, Multiset.card_erase_of_mem hp]` + `omega` instead of the five-step chain ending in `Nat.pred_eq_sub_one`.
findings.issue: `sum_splitCollinear` is a nine-step `rw` chain (`Multiset.sum_cons, Multiset.sum_cons, ← add_assoc, ← add_smul, add_sub_cancel, one_smul, ...`) whose middle four steps are just the reusable fact that a collinear pair sums to its parent, `z • p + (1 - z) • p = p`. `add_sub_cancel` is a name whose meaning has changed upstream (it is the `to_additive` of `mul_div_cancel : a * (b / a) = b`, Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Basic.lean:962), so the chain is rename-fragile and the physical content is invisible.

findings.evidence: Counterexamples.lean:113-116; `max_mul_of_nonneg (a b : R) (hc : 0 ≤ c) : max a b * c = max (a * c) (b * c)` at mathlib/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Ring/Unbundled/Basic.lean:457, i.e. the lemma rewrites the goal's RHS, not its LHS.
findings.fix: Insert the key step explicitly, e.g. `have key : max (z * E p) ((1 - z) * E p) = max z (1 - z) * E p := (max_mul_of_nonneg _ _ hp).symm`, then `simp [max_eq_left h₂, key]`.
findings.issue: `simp [max_mul_of_nonneg _ _ hp, max_eq_left h₂]` closes `max (E (z • p)) (max (E ((1 - z) • p)) 0) = max z (1 - z) * E p` by normalising both sides at once — it needs `map_smul`/`smul_eq_mul` from the default set and fires `max_mul_of_nonneg` left-to-right on the right-hand side. Nothing in the script shows the reader why it works.

summary: Proofs are mostly robust and readable, but `sum_splitCollinear` buries the reusable identity `z • p + (1 - z) • p = p` inside a nine-step named-lemma `rw` chain, and `leadingEnergy_splitCollinear_singleton` closes a non-obvious max/scalar computation entirely inside one `simp`.
